name: Topological Black Holes in Anti-de Sitter Space
description: Black holes in anti-de Sitter space whose horizons are planes, cylinders, tori, or closed surfaces of genus two or more, the static vacuum solutions with a negative cosmological constant over a surface of constant curvature. The flat one is the black brane of holography, and the hyperbolic one is a black hole even with no mass or a negative one.
convention: The anti-de Sitter radius $L$, a length, fixes the cosmological constant through $\Lambda = -3/L^2$. We keep factors of $c$ explicit.
history: Can a black hole be shaped like a doughnut? Stephen Hawking's answer of 1972 was no: he established that the horizon of a stationary black hole has the topology of a sphere [hawking1972, galloway1999]. His argument assumes that the energy density on the horizon is never negative, and a negative cosmological constant in vacuum breaks that assumption [galloway1999]. So in anti-de Sitter space a horizon may be a plane, a cylinder, a torus, or a closed surface with two or more handles, and the metric function is $$f(r) = k - \frac{\mu}{r} + \frac{r^2}{L^2},$$ with $k = 1$, $0$, or $-1$ for a horizon of positive, zero, or negative curvature [brill1997, birmingham1999]. At $k = 1$ it is the Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter black hole [brill1997].¶The flat hole came first, and it came out of two dimensions [lemos1995planar, birmingham1999]. José Lemos was working on the black holes of dilaton gravity in two dimensions over the winter of 1992/93 when he read one of them as a spacetime of four dimensions with the symmetry of a plane, "which is a planar black hole in General Relativity!" [lemos1995planar]. His cylindrical hole, which he also called a black string, has its horizon at $r_h = (\mu L^2)^{1/3}$ and its curvature singularity on the axis $r = 0$ [lemos1995]. Chao-Guang Huang and Can-Bin Liang built a charged hole whose surfaces of constant $t$ and $r$ are tori [huang1995]. Lemos and Vilson Zanchin gave the string rotation and charge, and closed it into a flat torus [lemos1996].¶And the pretzel? Cut a polygon of $4g$ sides from the hyperbolic plane, glue its edges in pairs, and you have a closed surface of genus $g \ge 2$, the simplest a regular octagon with opposite edges joined [aminneborg1996]. That is how Stefan Åminneborg, Ingemar Bengtsson, Sören Holst, and Peter Peldán made black holes with such horizons in 1996: they identified points of anti-de Sitter space, as Máximo Bañados, Marc Henneaux, Claudio Teitelboim, and Jorge Zanelli had done in three dimensions [aminneborg1996, banados1993]. Their spacetime is locally anti-de Sitter space, and they judged it "an amusing and perhaps an instructive footnote" [aminneborg1996]. Robert Mann gave these holes mass and charge, as a limit of the C-metric with a cosmological constant, and without charge his metric function is $f = -1 - \mu/r + r^2/L^2$ over a surface of area $4\pi(g - 1)r^2$ [mann1997].¶How light can a pretzel be? With $k = -1$ the horizon is there at $\mu = 0$, and it stays for negative mass down to $\mu = -2L/(3\sqrt{3})$, where $r_h = L/\sqrt{3}$ [mann1997negative, vanzo1997]. Between zero and that bound the hole has an inner horizon and a timelike singularity, and its conformal diagram is like that of the Reissner-Nordström black hole in anti-de Sitter space [mann1997negative, brill1997]. For every closed horizon, torus or pretzel, the entropy is a quarter of the area, by the Hamiltonian thermodynamics of Dieter Brill, Jorma Louko, and Peldán [brill1997]. These holes get hotter as they grow: the temperature is $$T = \frac{\hbar c}{4\pi k_B}\,\frac{3r_h^2 + kL^2}{L^2 r_h},$$ which rises with $r_h$ for $k = 0$ and $k = -1$, so the heat capacity is positive [brill1997]. In every dimension, Danny Birmingham found, these two kinds exist at every temperature, with no Hawking-Page transition [birmingham1999].¶Does a handle on the horizon break topological censorship? That theorem, proved by John Friedman, Kristin Schleich, and Donald Witt for asymptotically flat spacetimes, says that no observer who stays outside a black hole has time to probe the topology of spacetime [friedman1993]. Gregory Galloway, Schleich, Witt, and Eric Woolgar proved it again with a negative cosmological constant, and found that it bounds the genera $g_i$ of the horizons by the genus $g_0$ of infinity, $$\sum_i g_i \le g_0$$ [galloway1999]. A horizon with two handles needs a boundary at infinity with at least two [galloway1999]. The name topological black holes comes from the identifications, and Roberto Emparan kept it for horizons left as whole hyperbolic planes, "even if it will be somewhat of a misnomer" [emparan1999].¶The flat hole found a use in the correspondence between gravity in anti-de Sitter space and a field theory on its boundary, where it is that theory at a temperature in flat space, and in the coordinate $z = L^2/r$ the boundary is the plane $z = 0$ [witten1998thermal, hartnoll2009]. Pavel Kovtun, Dam Thanh Son, and Andrei Starinets found from such black branes that the dual fluid has $\eta/s = \hbar/(4\pi k_B)$, viscosity over entropy density, a value that "may serve as a lower bound for a wide class of systems" [kovtun2005]. Sean Hartnoll, Christopher Herzog, and Gary Horowitz built a superconductor on the flat hole of four dimensions by adding a charged scalar field [hartnoll2008]. The hyperbolic hole without mass is the part of anti-de Sitter space that a family of accelerated observers can reach, at the temperature $\hbar c/(2\pi k_B L)$ [vanzo1997, emparan1999]. Horacio Casini, Marina Huerta, and Robert Myers used the entropy of its horizon to compute the entanglement entropy across a sphere in the boundary theory [casini2011].

related.text: The member of the family with a round horizon, $k = 1$, where $\mu$ is the Schwarzschild radius $r_s$.
The hyperbolic hole without mass, $k = -1$ and $\mu = 0$, is anti-de Sitter space at every point. Its horizon is a black hole's once points are identified [aminneborg1996].
The black hole of three dimensions, made by identifying points of anti-de Sitter space. Åminneborg, Bengtsson, Holst, and Peldán repeated the construction in four [aminneborg1996].

coordinates.name: Static

parameters.description: Mass parameter, a length, equal to the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$ when $k = 1$
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$
Curvature of the horizon's own metric: $1$ for a sphere, $0$ for a plane, a cylinder or a torus, $-1$ for a hyperbolic plane or a closed surface of genus two or more

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \rho, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The surfaces of constant $t$ and $r$ have the metric $r^2\left(d\rho^2/(1 - k\rho^2) + \rho^2d\phi^2\right)$, of constant curvature $k/r^2$. The horizon $r_h$ is the largest root of $k - \mu/r + r^2/L^2$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(2r^3 + L^2\,\mu\right)\left(r^3 + k\,L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu\right)}{2L^4\,r^3}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{2r^3 + L^2\,\mu}{2r\left(r^3 + k\,L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r^3 + k\,L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu}{L^2\left(1 - k\,\rho^2\right)}\dot{\rho}^2 - \dfrac{\rho^2\left(r^3 + k\,L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu\right)}{L^2}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Mass parameter, a length, equal to the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$ when $k = 1$
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$
Curvature of the horizon's own metric: $1$ for a sphere, $0$ for a plane, a cylinder or a torus, $-1$ for a hyperbolic plane or a closed surface of genus two or more

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(v, r, \rho, \phi)$, with the advanced time $v = ct + r_*$ a length, where $dr_*/dr = \left(k - \mu/r + r^2/L^2\right)^{-1}$ and $r_* = 0$ at $r = 0$. The surfaces of constant $v$ and $r$ have the metric $r^2\left(d\rho^2/(1 - k\rho^2) + \rho^2d\phi^2\right)$, of constant curvature $k/r^2$. The horizon $r_h$ is the largest root of $k - \mu/r + r^2/L^2$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(2r^3 + L^2\,\mu\right)\left(r^3 + k\,L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu\right)}{2L^4\,r^3}\dot{v}^2 - \dfrac{2r^3 + L^2\,\mu}{L^2\,r^2}\dot{v}\dot{r} - \dfrac{r^3 + k\,L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu}{L^2\left(1 - k\,\rho^2\right)}\dot{\rho}^2 - \dfrac{\rho^2\left(r^3 + k\,L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu\right)}{L^2}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Mass parameter, a length, equal to the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$ when $k = 1$
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$
Curvature of the horizon's own metric: $1$ for a sphere, $0$ for a plane, a cylinder or a torus, $-1$ for a hyperbolic plane or a closed surface of genus two or more

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(u, r, \rho, \phi)$, with the retarded time $u = ct - r_*$ a length, where $dr_*/dr = \left(k - \mu/r + r^2/L^2\right)^{-1}$ and $r_* = 0$ at $r = 0$. The surfaces of constant $u$ and $r$ have the metric $r^2\left(d\rho^2/(1 - k\rho^2) + \rho^2d\phi^2\right)$, of constant curvature $k/r^2$. The horizon $r_h$ is the largest root of $k - \mu/r + r^2/L^2$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(2r^3 + L^2\,\mu\right)\left(r^3 + k\,L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu\right)}{2L^4\,r^3}\dot{u}^2 + \dfrac{2r^3 + L^2\,\mu}{L^2\,r^2}\dot{u}\dot{r} - \dfrac{r^3 + k\,L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu}{L^2\left(1 - k\,\rho^2\right)}\dot{\rho}^2 - \dfrac{\rho^2\left(r^3 + k\,L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu\right)}{L^2}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Black String

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \phi, z)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $\phi$ an angle around the string, and $z$ a length along it, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The horizon is the cylinder $r_h = (\mu L^2)^{1/3}$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(r^3 - L^2\,\mu\right)\left(2r^3 + L^2\,\mu\right)}{2L^4\,r^3}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{2r^3 + L^2\,\mu}{2r\left(r^3 - L^2\,\mu\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r^3 - L^2\,\mu}{L^2}\dot{\phi}^2 - \dfrac{r^3 - L^2\,\mu}{L^4}\dot{z}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Black Brane

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The length $z = L^2/r$, with $r$ the radius of the static chart at $k = 0$ and $r_h$ its value on the horizon, vanishes on the conformal boundary.

coordinates.name: Hyperbolic

parameters.description: Mass parameter, a length of either sign, no less than $-2L/(3\sqrt{3})$
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The surfaces of constant $t$ and $r$ are hyperbolic planes of curvature $-1/r^2$, or closed surfaces of genus two or more cut from them. The horizons $r_- < r_+$ are the positive roots of $-1 - \mu/r + r^2/L^2$, and $r_-$ exists only for $\mu < 0$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(2r^3 + L^2\,\mu\right)\left(r^3 - L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu\right)}{2L^4\,r^3}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{2r^3 + L^2\,\mu}{2r\left(r^3 - L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r^3 - L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu}{L^2}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^3 - L^2\,r - L^2\,\mu\right)\sinh^2\theta}{L^2}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0
